_readme: Phase 2 performance targets. CONFIGURABLE, because a target is a deployment
decision -- an on-prem cluster and a shared SaaS tier do not owe the same
latency -- and because a number hardcoded in a gate is one nobody can argue
These are AUTHORIZATION-PATH targets only: the deterministic decision that
runs synchronously because enforcement requires it. They deliberately do NOT
cover ingest, detection or correlation, which are asynchronous and whose
latency a caller never waits on.
A measurement satisfies a target only when the artifact BINDS to the build

rationale: Specification section 79. The gate is in front of every consequential
agent action, so its latency is added to work a human may be waiting on.
50 ms at p95 keeps it below the threshold at which an integrator starts
looking for a way to bypass it -- which is the real failure mode for an
inline control, not the milliseconds themselves.
authorization_decision.applies_when: no external network call is in the decision path

_note: A measurement is only interpretable against the machine that produced it.
The benchmark records CPU count, platform and Python version into its
artifact so a p95 from a laptop is never mistaken for a p95 from a
production node. The gate does NOT infer equivalence between machines --
it reports what was measured and where.
